title: Stanford study shows little evidence of health benefits from organic foods
summary: Stanford news release on a 2012 meta-analysis finding little evidence organic food is more nutritious or safer, though it lowers pesticide exposure, may carry more omega-3 in milk and fewer resistant bacteria in meat.

assertions.quote: They did not find strong evidence that organic foods are more nutritious or carry fewer health risks than conventional alternatives
There isn’t much difference between organic and conventional foods, if you’re an adult and making a decision based solely on your health
organic produce is 30 percent less likely to be contaminated with pesticides than conventional fruits and vegetables
the pesticide levels of all foods fell within the allowable safety limits.
organic milk may contain significantly higher levels of omega-3 fatty acids.
Organic foods are often twice as expensive as their conventionally grown counterparts.
did find lower levels of pesticide residues in the urine of children on organic diets
She emphasized the importance of eating of fruits and vegetables
organic chicken and pork appeared to reduce exposure to antibiotic-resistant bacteria

verdicts.note: The Stanford meta-analysis found about a third higher risk of multidrug-resistant bacteria on conventional chicken and pork, with unclear clinical significance.
